Caveat recorded: a radio-identical variant could in principle ship under a Class II permissive change, so this rules out a filed authorization, not the existence of the product; and a grant publishes frequencies, never port counts. research/ubiquiti-swx-grantee-census.md.  Then, 2026-11-19, the surface no earlier pass had read: Ubiquiti's own firmware index, `https://fw-update.ubnt.com/api/firmware?limit=1000&filter=eq~~product~~unifi-dream` -> HTTP 200, **340 releases across 17 platform codes** (`UDM`, `UDMPRO`, `UDMPROSE`, `UDMPROMAX`, `UDR`, `UDR5G`, `UDR7`, `UDRULT`, `UDW`, `UX`, `UXMAX`, `UCGF`, `UCGMAX`, `UCGA6AD`, `EFGCORE`, `UDMENT`, `UDMEA4C`), with `UDW` at 27 releases from 2022-05-07 to 2026-11-10 (latest `v6.0.17+7bcad58`, binary `/data/unifi-dream/2d04-UDW-6.0.17-…bin`) and **no `UDWPRO`**: the spellings `UDWPRO`, `UDW-PRO`, `UDWPROMAX`, `UDW2`, `UDWSE`, `UDWMAX` each return the 96-byte 0-release envelope, the same answer as the nonsense control `ZZZZ`, while `UDMPRO` returns 65, `UDMPROSE` 40 and `UDMPROMAX` 20 - three near-identical consoles that nevertheless carry three separate platform codes, which is why a shipped Pro Dream Wall would have its own. Caveat: a rebadged variant sharing the parent mainboard could hide under the `UDW` code, and no firmware index publishes port counts. research/ubiquiti-firmware-platform-census.md.
